name: Calibration assumptions
statement: For the 'estimated' calibration, the scatter per record (σe) and the shift per group (σu) are estimated by code from each analysis's frozen records with Henderson's method III, fixed at the rules lock: fit the locked model (RSS_R, rank r_R) and the same model with one intercept per group (RSS_F, rank r_F); σe² = RSS_F / (N - r_F); σu² = max(0, (RSS_R - RSS_F - (r_F - r_R) σe²) / tr(Z'M_R Z)). A negative estimate set to zero is recorded with its value before truncation. Not estimable (N <= r_F, RSS_F zero, or the trace zero): the estimated calibration of that analysis is 'unavailable' with the reason, and the fixed one is still reported. No person or agent chooses a value. A flag, never a gate.

name: What no plan can ever do to the primary set
statement: These hold for every plan, including any plan written by a model; no plan setting can change them. (1) An exact duplicate is never counted twice: one record of the group, chosen by the survivor rule, enters. (2) No record connected to a definite conflict ever enters, under any plan: not both records, not one. That includes a record linked by exact duplicates to a record in conflict (the whole connected group stays out). A survivor's value is counted only in the sensitivity analysis 'conflicts_survivor_value'. (3) A physically invalid value never enters. (4) A group whose identity cannot be resolved (several candidates) never enters; it is counted separately only in the sensitivity analysis 'possible_duplicates_separate'. (5) A model-recalled record never enters. (6) A constructed record (the controlled extract) never enters a run that is not marked as a test. (7) A record without a group under the plan's grouping never enters (no group is invented; entry 'records_without_group'). A plan that tries (1) to (4) is refused at the rules lock and refused again when its rules are applied; (5) is refused by the database; (6) by code at record storage, inclusion and the freeze; (7) by the eligibility rule 'group_unknown'. The one plan choice that remains: possible duplicates counted once (the default) or both counted. name: Sensitivity set without the group with the largest share of slope information
statement: The sensitivity set displayed "without the group with the largest share of slope information" (internal key 'without_most_influential_paper') is the primary set minus every record of the group under the plan's grouping (a paper, a dataset or a batch; the display states which) holding the largest share of slope information, I_g / Σ I_g, with I_g the group's sum of squared within-alloy deviations of the transformed grain size (entry 'effective_papers'), computed on the primary set's records. This is the largest share of within-alloy grain-size contrast, not necessarily the group whose removal changes the slope most: a group with much contrast whose outcomes lie close to the fitted line changes the slope little. The group is chosen by code at Inclusion from grain sizes, alloys and groups only, never from outcome values (Inclusion receives none). Shares within the numerical zero (RELATIVE_ZERO, 1e-10) of the largest are tied; a tie is broken by each tied group's earliest record under the plan's survivor source order, then the lowest row in the source file, then the stable identity (source-version fingerprint, origin key, item index), never a database id or an order. The removed records get the rule 'most_influential_paper' in that set only; it differs from the primary set in exactly this one respect (alloys left with one grain size are the fit's own 'not used in this fit', as in every set). Without any slope information nothing is removed. Descriptive only; it never changes the verdict.
